questions.title: Who will win Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election?
questions.background: Okinawa is Japan's southernmost prefecture, where the presence of US military bases is a major political issue.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official results announced by Okinawa's election authorities, either directly or as reported by reliable news organizations. Resolution : The question resolves when the winner of Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major final-weekend polling sweep published Sept 6 (one week before Sept 13 voting) shifts the race decisively toward five-party-backed challenger Genta Koja (0.53 -> 0.63) over two-term All-Okinawa incumbent Denny Tamaki (0.46 -> 0.365; 0.005 across four minor candidates): (1) Yomiuri Shimbun (Sep 3-6, phone+net, n=1,410) reports Koja clearly leading ('先行') with Tamaki trailing—noting 20% of 2022 Tamaki voters switched to Koja, 80% of 2022 Shimoji voters back Koja, and economy/prices (75%) dwarfs bases (45%); (2) Asahi Shimbun / Okinawa Times / QAB (Sep 5-6, phone+net) similarly reports Koja slightly ahead ('やや先行') with Tamaki chasing vigorously (40% undecided)—a striking signal given Okinawa Times/Asahi's historically All-Okinawa-favorable coverage; (3) Kyodo / Ryukyu Shimpo / OTV (Sep 5-6, pure RDD phone, 603 landline + 404 mobile) shows a dead heat ('横一線', <10% undecided), yet its internals also favor Koja: economy/tourism/jobs is the #1 issue (46%, breaking 70% Koja) vs bases (26%, breaking 80% Tamaki), and Henoko relocation support edges opposition 48%-46%. We cap Koja at 0.63 (leaving Tamaki 0.365) because pure phone polls remain tied, Tamaki leads ~60% of independents and 70+ voters (who turn out at higher rates), and 20-40% remain undecided in Yomiuri/Asahi.

questions.current_reasoning: Upgrading Camp Nou (0.56 -> 0.65) over Wembley Stadium (0.44 -> 0.35) in this confirmed two-stadium race decided by the UEFA Executive Committee on Sep 14-15, 2026. An Aug 27 Football Ground Guide report explicitly states that the revamped ~105,000-seat Camp Nou is now considered the 'clear favourite' for the 2029 Champions League final following a major UEFA shift and improving relations between Joan Laporta and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin. questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-06 check (Exa + Sept 2 Reuters/Straits Times investigation 'US, China arm for space warfare: hunter satellites and orbital weapons'): No country has yet publicly acknowledged already-deployed orbital weapons. Crucially, the Sept 2 Reuters report sharpens the asymmetry in public-acknowledgment propensity: China's Foreign Ministry reiterated on the record that Beijing opposes space weaponization and insists its spaceplane/Shiyan missions are peaceful/experimental, and Moscow continues denying its nuclear ASAT program. By contrast, US SPACECOM head Gen. Stephen Whiting is openly arguing for an active warfighting posture and orbital interceptors, incoming Space Force CSO Lt. Gen. Douglas Schiess led the newly disclosed US-UK orbital proximity operation, and the Space Force already broke silence in June with a rare disclosure of an earthbound L3Harris ASAT jammer—building toward potential deterrence disclosures at the mid-September AFA Air, Space & Cyber Conference. Lifting United States (0.49 -> 0.53) while trimming Russia (0.25 -> 0.23) and China (0.12 -> 0.10), with France (0.08, Yoda) and India (0.03) steady (sum = 0.97).

questions.title: Which club will win the 2026 Campeones Cup?
questions.background: The Campeones Cup is an annual match between the previous season’s MLS Cup champion and the winner of Mexico’s Campeón de Campeones.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official competition result published by Major League Soccer, supported by reliable match reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the club officially declared the winner of the 2026 Campeones Cup once the match has concluded, including extra time or a penalty shootout if required. Accepted Answer Format : The winning club’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Modestly trimming Inter Miami CF (-0.03 to 0.55) and lifting Cruz Azul (+0.03 to 0.45) ahead of the Sept 16 single-leg Campeones Cup final at Nu Stadium following Miami's Sept 5/6 MLS result and a full September schedule comparison. Although Lionel Messi stayed sharp in his first match since retiring from Argentina (2 assists, crossbar free kick) and Casemiro plus Luis Suarez scored, Miami were held 2-2 at home by lowly Atlanta United (6-13-3, 21 pts)—conceding two goals and two penalties (one saved by Dayne St. Clair, one scored by Breel Embolo in the 87') with Casemiro deployed at center-back, leaving Miami with just one win in their last seven MLS matches. Moreover, verified September calendars show Inter Miami face heavier pre-final congestion (4 matches in 11 days: Sept 5 Atlanta after a 90-min lightning delay, Sept 9 away at playoff-contending Chicago Fire, Sept 12 vs Eastern Conference-leading Nashville SC [16-2-4], then Sept 16 Cruz Azul), whereas 10th-placed Cruz Azul (3W-3L, playing winless Santos Laguna tonight Sept 6) have no midweek game before their Sept 12 Clasico Joven vs Liga MX leaders Club America. Miami remain deserved ~55% favorites on home soil with a non-traveling Messi and Cruz Azul's America/travel/Monterrey (Sept 19) rotation dilemma reported by AS Mexico, but 0.55/0.45 better prices Miami's defensive fragility and veteran fatigue.

questions.title: Who will top the PSA women's world squash rankings on September 21, 2026?
questions.background: The Professional Squash Association (PSA) publishes weekly world rankings for professional squash players.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official PSA women's world rankings dated September 21, 2026. Resolution : Resolve to the player ranked first in that rankings update. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-09-06 update after a dramatic Gold-level London Squash Classic finish at Alexandra Palace: on Sept 5, World No. 1 Hania El Hammamy suffered a shock 3-1 semi-final upset to England's No. 5 Georgina Kennedy (11-6, 14-12, 7-11, 11-8—Kennedy's first win in 26 tries vs a top-3 player and first in 10 vs El Hammamy, after El Hammamy barely scraped past Amanda Sobhy 13-11 in the third in the QFs). Today (Sept 6), World No. 2 Amina Orfi—having swept nemesis Sivasangari Subramaniam 3-0 in the SFs—crushed Kennedy 3-0 (11-6, 11-8, 11-2) to defend her London title and retain her full 1,750 Gold winner points. London was supposed to be El Hammamy's opportunity to pad her slim cushion over Orfi (who finished 2025/26 winning the World Championships and British Open and came within one match of #1 at June's Tour Finals) before El Hammamy faces heavy mid-September 2025 defending points and a tough Platinum QTerminals Qatar Classic (Sept 12-18) draw featuring returning former No. 1 Nouran Gohar in the quarter-finals. Instead, El Hammamy banked only 700 SF points while showing clear early-season rust, whereas Orfi opened 2026/27 in imperious form. We compress El Hammamy sharply 0.63 -> 0.51 and raise Orfi 0.35 -> 0.48 (trimming London-skipper Nour El Sherbini 0.015 -> 0.01), keeping El Hammamy a razor-thin favorite pending tomorrow's (Sept 7) official PSA points-gap update and her 90.4% 2025/26 win rate as defending Qatar champion.
